content: This medication is prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your healthcare provider. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Any unused portion should be discarded after 14 days. Do not dispose of this medication by flushing it down the toilet or pouring it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is a cephalosporin-type antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including those affecting the middle ear, skin, urinary tract, and respiratory tract. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Shake the bottle well before each dose. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically every 8 or 12 hours. For optimal effectiveness, take it at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include stomach upset, headache, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cefaclor may interfere with live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, reducing their effectiveness. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is known to pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
